producer_report.summary: A weekly or session limit reply ("You've hit your weekly limit · resets Nov 12, 3pm") is now classified as a usage-limit environment stop, and `athena drain` stops on the first such job with the reason "usage limit" and the reset time. The fix is in the shared classifier. Before it, only "API Error: 429" counted as a usage limit, so this text closed the job as "the producer did not complete" and counted against its line. `usage_limit_hit` in claude.rs reads the reply. It matches only an error result of subtype success or error whose text starts with the sentence, so a model's own prose, or the same words under error_max_turns, stays a work failure. disk.rs's `producer_stop_reason` and `StopCause::of` call it through a new `is_usage_limit`. The reset time stays inside the existing reason string (`usage_limit_reset` reads it back), so no record kind is added. In drain.rs, `Stop::UsageLimit` (label "usage limit") is set in `run_job` at the first failed job with that cause, with no second attempt, plus a note "usage limit reached; it resets <time>". main.rs help gets the new stop line. CHANGELOG.md has an entry. Behaviour change beyond the brief: a bare 429 now also stops the drain at its first job, not after the item fails twice, so the old drain test for 429 was narrowed to low disk. producer.rs, display.rs, resumable_stop, keeps_unfinished_work and retry are untouched. Follow-up: a limit hit in a reader, verifier or planner call keeps its current handling, as a 429 does today.

open_issues: Host: the exact wording and subtype the real Claude Code CLI emits for a weekly or session limit are not visible in the repository. I assumed an is_error result with subtype `success` whose text starts "You've hit your weekly|session limit · resets <time>". If the live CLI differs, only `usage_limit_hit` needs adjusting; a captured real reply would settle it.

Deliberate behaviour change: a bare 429 now also ends the drain at its first failed job with the new `usage limit` stop, not as `Stop::Environment` after the item failed twice. The old drain test was narrowed to low disk.
Only the producer stage maps a limit reply to an environment stop; a limit hit in a reader, verifier or planner call keeps its current handling, which is the existing 429 scope. Follow-up if wanted.
With max_concurrency above 1, jobs already running finish, and each worker that hits the limit adds its own note; `set_stop` keeps the first stop.
mistakes: My first stand-in script used a literal apostrophe inside single quotes. That broke the shell script and failed two tests; I fixed it by splicing the apostrophe.
The first clippy run flagged `single_element_loop` in the narrowed low-disk drain test; fixed by removing the loop.
learnings: `disk.rs` is the single classifier of environment reasons. The scope guard and `athena retry` read it, and `drain` reads it through `StopCause::of`, so one change there reaches all of them.
`scope_guard::counted` is private and keyed on the attempt verdict, so a run-level test can assert only `is_environment_reason` as the proof that the guard does not count the job.

In the claude.rs stand-in script, an apostrophe inside a shell single-quoted JSON line breaks the script; splice it as `'\''`. The tool also turned a `'` escape I typed in that script into a literal apostrophe.
Bash hooks here deny pipes, `git -C`, and double-quoted expansions; use `--manifest-path` and the `-q` flag to keep cargo output small.
`Stop::ALL`, `label`, `meaning`, and the drain `after_help` text in main.rs must all list a new `Stop`; the test `drain_help_documents_the_flags_and_lists_every_stop_reason` enforces it.
desires: A captured real weekly/session-limit reply from the live CLI to confirm the subtype and wording.
A way to read long cargo output files from the tool-results directory; the policy blocks reads outside the working directory.
